title: Trailers vs Clones, copies, and ripoffs
author: House13Games
selftext: Classic indie development has always recommended building community and awareness as you go along, and to start the marketing early. Does that advice still apply today, when AI can clone stuff from a pic or a trailer and slop out some shit clones before you can get your handcrafted masterpiece over the finish line?

replies.author: House13Games
replies.body: That doesn't soound so great either. Is the new strategy to keep quiet until you have the product ready to launch, then push it real hard and fast?

replies.author: _Vultrix_
replies.body: Yep or close to ready. But honestly it’s the death of small games in general unless they’re really high quality handmade and stuff that ai can’t currently replicate.

replies.author: House13Games
replies.body: I have a pretty high quality game, which has a number of innovative ideas and a certain vibe. Although it's taken me ages, I am terrified AI can slop out a cheap low quality copy, and I wouldn't be first on the market any more. They used to say ideas are worthless and it's the execution that counts, but I'm seeing the barrier to execution disappear completely. Unique ideas are going to become very valuable, I think. Finally the Ideas Guy gets to do their thing!

replies.author: Key-Media-6395
replies.body:
For more context, AI can copy games, but it doesn't do a good job unless the game is very simple mechanically, or the person leading the AI has a good idea of what they are doing.

The most well known AI copies are all very mechanically simple games, (needle in a haystack, that wall mining game, ect) while AI CAN copy more complicated games, its not going to do a very good job, unless the person copying you is able to put enough effort into the game to make sure that it is actually fun to play. and, while its still not \*good\* having an AI copy your game gets your more publicity. 

Chances also are, your game will not get copied. i'd say 90% of the people using AI for game dev are not bad actors, and those who are, are going to be looking for the newest, viral thing. 

All AI is doing is lowering the difficulty threshold of who gets to make Things. People have always been making rip offs, and slop, but its easier to do so now. As long as you are consistent and are able to actually get your game out, you'll be better off than the people who don't advertise. Honestly, with the amount of people choosing not to market, it might decongest the indie game space a little bit... though thats probably countered by the amount of low quality AI games.

comments.author: Agile_Branch_8743
comments.body: Very few games have a truly original idea. If yours has a better implementation than the copies, the key is to help it reach its audience and to release it as soon as possible. Either way, based on most projects shared here, AIs are too busy ripping popular projects off.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
yes, it is still the same. 

we are in the age of social media. 

fame and money start with views and clicks. 

gotta chase those views and clicks. 

I mean, sure, you can "lose the game" because a clone takes all your views and clicks. 

or you can just lose because your game has no views and clicks. 

very simple situation
